app.summary: Offline file conversion, compression and metadata scrubbing
headline: Your photos know
where you live.
app.lede: Shrink files, change their format, and strip what they carry — GPS, camera serial, the thumbnail of the uncropped original. Shown to you first, then removed. No file ever leaves your Mac.
app.meta: macOS 15+ · Apple silicon · free & open source

features.title: Watch it work.
features.body: A folder of photos, a document and a video — dropped in as one archive, planned, renamed, and run. No narration, no cuts, nothing sped up. That is the whole app.

features.title: The app proposes a plan.
features.body: Files land and trinket reads them, works out what it would do, and shows the whole path at once — open the archive, shrink the photos, convert the video, pack it back up. Every decision already answered. Change what you like, press one button.

features.title: A scrub nobody can verify is just a promise.
features.body: Photos carry more than they look like they carry: coordinates, the camera's serial, the software, sometimes the machine that edited them. A cropped photo can keep a thumbnail of the uncropped original — so cropping someone out and sharing it leaks them anyway. trinket shows what it found, on a map, before removing anything.

features.title: "I zipped my photos and it got bigger."
features.body: Because JPEG, MP4 and PDF have no redundancy left. Zipping them adds container overhead — 145.3 MB came out at 146.7 MB, slowly. Compressing harder only makes it slower. So trinket opens the archive, re-encodes what is inside, and packs it back up. Same photos: 73.8 MB.

features.title: It tells you what it could not do.
features.body: A file trinket cannot improve is named and marked, never given a progress bar that never moves. A batch that saved nothing says so rather than printing 0%. macOS re-injects a producer name into every PDF it writes, so the strongest scrub cannot fully clean one — and the app says that where you choose it.

install.title: Three lines.
install.note: Builds with the Swift toolchain from the Command Line Tools. No Xcode. The app is ad-hoc signed, so a downloaded build is blocked by Gatekeeper unless you clear it by hand — building from the clone avoids that entirely. Bundles ffmpeg, which is why trinket is GPL-3.
